flashcard_questions.q: How many universities are there in Liverpool?
How many students study in Liverpool?
How many international students study in Liverpool?
How much do students spend in Liverpool each year?
What is the multiplier effect in urban regeneration?
flashcard_questions.a: When one new development triggers further growth and investment in the area.

flashcard_questions.q: When was Liverpool the European Capital of Culture?
How much extra money did the Capital of Culture award generate for Liverpool?
How many visitors came to Liverpool in its Capital of Culture year?
By what percentage did visitor numbers to Liverpool rise that year?
Which Liverpool area has had derelict homes refurbished and rebuilt?
What is brownfield land in planning?
flashcard_questions.a: Land that has previously been built on, such as old factories.

flashcard_questions.q: What is urban greening in a city?
flashcard_questions.a: Creating green natural spaces within a city, for example parks and street trees.

flashcard_questions.q: What lies directly beneath Chavasse Park in Liverpool?
How do the trees in Chavasse Park improve Liverpool's air quality?
flashcard_questions.a: They act as a carbon sink, absorbing carbon dioxide from traffic.

flashcard_questions.q: How large is Sefton Park in Liverpool?

notes: 15 cards: 4 term-to-definition (multiplier effect, brownfield land, urban greening, carbon sink through the Chavasse card), 9 case-study-to-fact naming Liverpool or the park with one figure each (11 universities, 50,000 students, 11,000 international, £1 billion, 2008, £800 million, 28 million visitors, 35%, 2,000-space car park, 235 acres), 1 place card (Anfield), 1 cause-to-consequence (trees and air quality). The £4 million tree planting budget, Stanley Park, green corridors and inclusive design were trimmed to stay within 15.
